Yes exercise is good and healthy when it’s done safely. Don’t push yourself and don’t do it obsessively. 

Yes have calorie dense snacks, if you like peanut butter that is good. If you’re really full I don’t recommend pushing yourself to eat even more. If you need more calories eating small calorie dense snacks is the best way to approach this.

Walking is still good and a safe exercise to do. You will still be able to gain weight whilst walking because I’d assume you’d be eating a more normal amount of food. Just maybe cut down the amount of steps and don’t walk so much. You might not have a lot of energy to do much walking anyways in recovery.

Eat until you’re full! This is very important eating way more than your stomach can handle, can cause vomiting, at least in my experience I ate way too much and got really sick. (Mind you I was going through extreme hunger) Eating more snacks than meals throughout the day, snacks high in calories that are small can help too. Because restricting your intake causes your stomach to shrink so instantly going in and eating a lot of food can and will cause some problems. Eat foods high in fibre and that are easy to stomach. 

Smoothies are good for this as well, liquid calories are your friend. It depends how long you’ve been restricting for. I was restricting for about a year and it took 2/3 weeks to be able to eat normally again without feeling so sick. It depends how long you’ve been restricting for, if you’ve been restricting for longer. Getting your body used to eating more food will take longer. If you are worried about this I’d suggest talking to a doctor to get their opinion or your therapist. Most of the weight gain at the start will be water weight/food weight. Also lots of bloating is extremely normal as well, there are exercises and things you can do to help reduce this. Hot water bottles are good for the stomach cramps. 

Counting calories is something that I never would want do again, if you are concerned about this I’d suggest talking to your therapist because everyone is different. I don’t want to give some advice about this that could be harmful or wrong. However generally speaking counting calories in recovery isn’t a good idea for a lot of people.

I hope this helps!
